title: bug: the ps1 wrapper runs a whitespace-only qualityGate and rescues every completion, while the sh twin and the policy see no gate
description:
Found by the Wave 1 integration gate (task-808869c5, adversarial pass). The two wrappers read settings.qualityGate differently:
- sh trims it (`v.strip()` where the post-flight reads the setting).
- delivery/policy.ts trims it (requiredCheckCommand).
- ps1 stores it verbatim: `$s.qualityGate = $qg` in Read-MoeCommitSettings.

Consequences:
1. Whitespace-only value (a hand-edited `"qualityGate": "   "`). sh and the policy see no gate. ps1 sees a truthy string, and this happens on every completion:
   - Invoke-MoeFrozenGate runs `cmd /d /s /c "   "`.
   - record_check_run refuses the blank command, so Send-MoeCheckRun throws 'qualityGate check persistence failed'.
   - The landing becomes MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE: a rescue ref, a "PUSH-BLOCKED: qualityGate failed ... (exit 0)" line, and the worker loop stops.
2. Padded value ("  node gate.cjs  "). ps1 records the check command padded, and the policy compared it exactly, so a PASSING gate withheld dependents and refused qa_approve. The pilot reproduced this: `node scripts/tests/wave1-pilot.mjs --gate-command "  node gate.cjs  "`. task-808869c5 fixed it consumer-side (policy.ts now compares the trimmed recorded command), but the evidence ps1 records is still not canonical.
3. Parity nit: the sh gate-failure line is "🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED: …", the marker the role docs use. The ps1 chat line and task comment lack the 🚫 prefix.
definitionOfDone: scripts/moe-agent.ps1 trims settings.qualityGate when it reads it, exactly as the sh twin does: a whitespace-only value means no gate, and a padded one runs and records the trimmed command
A frozen-candidate mode in both postflight twins lands a completion under a whitespace-only qualityGate with no candidate, no check run and no rescue ref, and that mode fails on the pre-fix ps1
The ps1 gate-failure chat line and task comment carry the same '🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED:' marker as the sh twin, pinned by parity-check.{sh,ps1}
postflight.sh, postflight.ps1 (pwsh and PS 5.1) and both parity checks pass

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 1+2 — confirm the three spots and record baselines. No repo edits.

Verified while planning; re-check by grep, never by line number:
- ps1 `Read-MoeCommitSettings`: `$qg = Get-MoeProp $st 'qualityGate'` followed by `if ($qg -is [string]) { $s.qualityGate = $qg }` — stored verbatim. Its neighbour `consolidationBranch` already trims and already treats a whitespace-only value as unset, so qualityGate is the outlier in its own function.
- sh: the post-flight settings reader prints `v.strip() if isinstance(v, str) else ''`, and every later use is `[ -n "${QUALITY_GATE:-}" ]`. So sh already behaves the way this card wants ps1 to.
- The gate-failure chat line: sh builds `🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED: qualityGate failed for task …`, ps1 builds the same sentence WITHOUT the marker, and both parity lists pin only the bare substring `PUSH-BLOCKED:`, which is why the difference survived. Note that the OTHER PUSH-BLOCKED line in both twins (the post-flight status-lookup one) carries no marker in either — leave that pair alone.
- ps1 feeds the same `$gateMsg` to the chat line and to the add_comment body, so one edit fixes both halves of DoD 3.

Also check, before writing any arm: the frozen suite's existing `pushBlocked` helper matches on `includes('PUSH-BLOCKED')`, so prefixing the marker must not disturb it. Say so in the step note after reading it.

Baselines with counts and exit codes: `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`, and both ps1 twins launched from PowerShell under pwsh and powershell.exe (mem:gotcha-ps-harness-ctrlc-from-git-bash).
implementationPlan.note:
No repo edits. Confirmed by grep on HEAD bb5e7e2 (scripts/ unchanged since 7728e7b, clean vs HEAD):
- ps1 Read-MoeCommitSettings: `$qg = Get-MoeProp $st 'qualityGate'` then `if ($qg -is [string]) { $s.qualityGate = $qg }` (verbatim); neighbour consolidationBranch trims. Downstream: gate decision `if ($Kind -eq 'completion' -and $RunGate -and $Settings.qualityGate)`, Invoke-MoeFrozenGate `if (-not $Command) { return $true }`, Send-MoeCheckRun `command=$Gate.Command`, `$gateMsg="PUSH-BLOCKED: qualityGate failed ..."` (feeds chat AND add_comment).
- sh: post-flight reader `print(v.strip() if isinstance(v, str) else '')`; uses `[ -n "${QUALITY_GATE:-}" ]`; announce_gate_failure builds `🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED: ...`. Status-lookup PUSH-BLOCKED line unmarked in both twins (left alone).
- Parity lists pin bare 'PUSH-BLOCKED:' (parity-check.sh:62, parity-check.ps1:53).
- Frozen suite pushBlocked helper = `includes('PUSH-BLOCKED')` on chat rows + add_comment; the scenario greps (postflight.ps1 Q/gate-fail -notlike '*PUSH-BLOCKED: qualityGate failed for task task-postflight*', postflight.sh grep -Fq same) and wave1-pilot.mjs:474 are substring matches: a leading marker disturbs none.
- The fake daemon's record_check_run refuses a blank command like the real one (`args.command.trim()`), and logs refused calls too.
EXTRA FINDING (shapes step 3c): parity-check.ps1 has no BOM (CRLF) and reads both wrappers with bare `Get-Content -Raw`. On PS 5.1 (ANSI = Windows-1252) the BOM-less moe-agent.sh decodes the emoji as mojibake: IndexOf('🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED:') = -1 with the default read, 93655 with -Encoding UTF8 (pwsh 7: 93655 both). So the ps1 list must build the marker from its code point and read the wrappers as UTF-8. moe-agent.ps1 HAS a BOM, so its literal is safe on both engines; ConvertTo-Json + Invoke-MoeRpc's UTF-8 OutputEncoding keep the surrogate pair intact on both.
Hot-reload hazard: every repo-launched ps1 wrapper restarts on a moe-agent.ps1 hash change, so the fix must be parse-checked on both engines right after the edit. A peer postflight.sh runs from the repo; bash reads scripts by offset, so repo harness edits go in via atomic rename, never in place.
BASELINES (scratch copy D:/moe-t8fc3/base = HEAD scripts): parity-check.sh PASS exit 0 (6m35s, MSYS forks slow under load); parity-check.ps1 PASS exit 0 on pwsh 7.6.6 and PS 5.1. Frozen count 64 sh / 64 ps1 (computed from the modes array), scope 28 (808869c5 recorded 64+28 PASS on these exact bytes). Full ps1/pwsh harness baseline: exit 1 at frozen race-pass, run.signal SIGTERM at the 180 s budget, stalled inside its 2nd gate run: load, not code (node -e 0 = 2.3 s, git --version = 4.6 s, py in %TEMP% = 6.5 s; ~60 moe-next vitest workers + a peer postflight.sh). Full-harness runs deferred to step 4 with a higher MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC; any failure there is classified against the base copy.
17 dirty paths belong to others; not touched.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 3 — two frozen arms first, byte-identical in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1. Edit with the Edit tool (mem:gotcha-serena-edit-rewrites-crlf-on-windows, mem:gotcha-bash-tool-json-escapes-generated-code).

- `gate-blank`: the fixture's project.json carries `"qualityGate": "   "` on an ordinary gated-shape completion. Assert the landing behaves exactly as a no-gate completion does: a commit on the branch, ZERO record_candidate rows, ZERO record_check_run rows, no rescue ref under refs/moe/rescue/, no PUSH-BLOCKED line anywhere (chat or comment), finalize outcome `landed`, and the loop not stopped.
- `gate-padded`: `"qualityGate": "  node gate.cjs  "`. Assert the gate RUNS and that the recorded check command is exactly `node gate.cjs` — the trimmed string, byte-compared, because the delivery policy's required-check token is built from the trimmed command and a padded record is what withheld dependents from a passing gate.

Both arms assert on the wrapper log they captured, so a failure shows what the wrapper actually printed. Error handling inside the arms: a mode that cannot read the fixture's records fails with that log attached rather than silently asserting on an empty list, which is how a vacuous green slips through.

Red proof, one run per mode (`MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY=<mode>`, ps1 from PowerShell):

Record the first failing assertion for each ps1 arm.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4 — the fix, in scripts/moe-agent.ps1, plus the marker parity in both checks.

(a) Read-MoeCommitSettings: trim the value as it is read, so a whitespace-only setting means NO gate and a padded one becomes canonical. One comment saying the sh twin's settings reader and delivery/policy.ts both trim, so this is the third copy of one rule and the wrapper's recorded evidence is the one that must be canonical.

Everything downstream then inherits it with no further edits: the truthiness test that decides whether a completion gates, the command the frozen gate runs, the command recorded on the check run, and the text in the failure line. Do not add a second trim at any of those sites — one rule, one place.

Error handling for this change, which is small but real: keep the existing `-is [string]` guard so a missing, null or non-string setting never reaches Trim() and still falls through to the default empty gate; a malformed project.json is already swallowed by the enclosing try/catch that leaves the defaults standing, and this edit must not move that boundary. The result is that every failure mode of the setting now lands on 'no gate configured' instead of on a blank command the daemon refuses.

(b) The gate-failure message: prefix the ps1 `$gateMsg` with the same `🚫 ` marker the sh twin uses, which covers both the chat line and the task comment since they share the string. Leave the post-flight status-lookup PUSH-BLOCKED line alone: neither twin marks that one, and marking one of them would create the very asymmetry this card is closing.

(c) scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1: replace the bare `PUSH-BLOCKED:` chat-prefix entry with `🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED:` in BOTH lists, so the marker itself is pinned rather than just the words after it. Prove the guard once: delete the marker from one wrapper, confirm BOTH parity scripts fail, restore it.

Watch the encoding: both harness and wrapper files must keep their current encoding and line endings. Check `git diff --numstat` shows only the expected lines and that the emoji survives a round trip in PowerShell 5.1 as well as pwsh — an emoji written as literal bytes by a tool that rewrites the file as ANSI would break the parity check on the other engine.

Both arms from step 2 turn green on ps1 and stay green on sh.

(a) moe-agent.ps1:1980 Read-MoeCommitSettings now does `if ($qg -is [string]) { $s.qualityGate = $qg.Trim() }`, plus the three-line comment the plan asked for.

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 7+8 — self-review, then complete. Answer in ONE task comment:
1. One rule, one place: show the trim happens where the setting is read and nowhere else, and list what inherits it (the gate decision, the executed command, the recorded check command, the failure text).
2. The three readers now agree: ps1, the sh settings reader and delivery/policy.ts. Say what each does with `"   "` and with `"  node gate.cjs  "`.
3. What the padded case cost before the fix: a PASSING gate recorded a padded command, the policy compared it exactly, and dependents were withheld. task-808869c5 fixed the consumer side; this card makes the evidence canonical at the source. Say whether both halves are now needed or whether one is redundant — and keep both regardless, since a consumer-side trim protects records already on disk.
4. Honest reds: `gate-blank` and `gate-padded` were red on ps1 only; on sh they were green from the start and are parity guards. Do not present them as a two-engine red.
5. The marker: both twins now build the same sentence, both parity lists pin the marker, and the status-lookup PUSH-BLOCKED line is deliberately unmarked in both.
6. Encoding: confirm the emoji survives in both PowerShell engines and that `git diff --numstat` shows no unrelated churn.
7. Would I be embarrassed if this broke in production? Name the worst case — a project whose gate silently stops running because of an over-eager trim — and which arm would catch it.

Then: call moe.declare_files for exactly the five files this plan names, and moe.complete_task with verification `{ command: 'MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh', exitCode: 0, outputTail }` plus a summary carrying the two arms, the ps1 results for both engines and both parity results.

comments.content:
Self-review for task-8fc35d31 (plan step 5)

1. One rule, one place.
- The trim happens at scripts/moe-agent.ps1:1980 in Read-MoeCommitSettings: `if ($qg -is [string]) { $s.qualityGate = $qg.Trim() }`.
- That is the file's only qualityGate reader. grep finds no other Trim on the gate.
- Everything downstream inherits it:
  - the gate decision `$Settings.qualityGate` (3799);
  - `$gate` (3802), which becomes Invoke-MoeFrozenGate's `$Command`, the command actually executed;
  - Send-MoeCheckRun's `command=$Gate.Command`, the recorded check;
  - `$gateMsg`, the failure text.
- The `-is [string]` guard is kept, so null or non-string values still fall to the default ''. The malformed-JSON try/catch boundary is unchanged.

2. The three readers now agree.
- `"   "`:
  - ps1 Trim() gives '', so no gate.
  - The sh reader's `v.strip()` gives '', so `[ -n ]` is false and there is no gate.
  - policy.ts:167 `settings.qualityGate.trim()` gives '', so there is no required check.
- `"  node gate.cjs  "`: all three give `node gate.cjs`.
  - ps1 and sh run and record that string.
  - The policy builds `required-check:node gate.cjs` from it and matches it with `run.command.trim() === command` (policy.ts:190).
- Residual, theoretical only. I measured the three whitespace sets; .NET Trim is identical on pwsh 7 and PS 5.1.
  - They agree on space, tab, CR, LF, VT, FF, U+00A0, U+2028 and U+3000.
  - They differ only on exotic characters: U+0085 (JS keeps it), U+001C-1F (only Python strips them) and U+FEFF (only JS strips it).
  - Not fixed. It is not a realistic hand-edit, and policy.ts's consumer trim still covers U+FEFF.

3. What the padded case cost, and whether both halves are needed.
- Before the fix, a PASSING ps1 gate recorded `  node gate.cjs  `. The policy compared that exactly against its trimmed token, so the passing check never counted: dependents were withheld and qa_approve refused.
- task-808869c5 fixed the consumer side (`run.command.trim()`). This card makes the evidence canonical at the source.
- For new ps1 records, the consumer trim is now redundant. KEEP BOTH anyway:
  - The consumer trim protects padded records already on disk, and any future writer.
  - The source trim keeps the record honest. It is also the only half that fixes the blank case, which was never a comparison problem: ps1 RAN `cmd /d /s /c "   "`, the daemon's record_check_run refused the blank command, and the landing became MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE plus a rescue ref, on every completion.

4. Honest reds: these were red on ps1 ONLY. Pre-fix wrapper, pwsh, one run per mode:
- gate-blank failed with "the worker loop must go on claiming after this exit". The log shows `Post-flight: quality gate:    `, then the fake record_check_run refusing the blank command, `qualityGate check persistence failed`, `MOE_RESCUE_REF ... reason=gate-failed`, and no second claim.
- gate-padded: recorded [['  node gate.cjs  ',0]] where [['node gate.cjs',0]] was expected.
- dirty-helper (the new exact-marker line): {chat:false, comment:false}.
- On sh all three were GREEN before the fix (PASS 3, 74 s). There they are parity guards, not reds.

5. The marker.
- Both twins now build the same sentence: `🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED: qualityGate failed for task <id>: <gate> (exit <rc>)`. ps1's `$gateMsg` feeds both the chat line and the add_comment body.
- Both parity lists now pin `🚫 PUSH-BLOCKED:` instead of the bare words.
- The guard was proven both ways, on sh, pwsh and PS 5.1:
  - marker missing from ps1 (the pre-fix repo): both parity scripts fail;
  - marker missing from sh (a scratch tree; the repo copy was never touched): both fail.
- The status-lookup `PUSH-BLOCKED:` line stays unmarked in both twins, deliberately.

6. Encoding.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The fix is one trim at the point of reading, not a guard at each use. ps1 already trims consolidationBranch in the same function, sh trims in its settings reader, and delivery/policy.ts trims when it builds the required-check token — so trimming at the read makes the wrapper's recorded evidence canonical and leaves exactly one rule per twin.

- Rejected: guarding each use site (the gate decision, the executed command, the recorded command). Three guards drift; one read does not.
- Rejected: fixing this consumer-side only. task-808869c5 already made policy.ts compare the trimmed recorded command, which protects records already on disk, but a padded record is still wrong evidence and the whitespace-only case is not a comparison problem at all — ps1 RUNS `cmd /d /s /c "   "` and turns every completion into a rescue.
- Rejected: touching the post-flight status-lookup PUSH-BLOCKED line. Neither twin marks it; marking one would create a new asymmetry.
- Rejected: adding a daemon-side refusal for a whitespace-only qualityGate. The setting is a project file a human edits, the daemon already refuses a blank check command, and this card is wrapper parity.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- ps1 Read-MoeCommitSettings stores qualityGate verbatim while trimming consolidationBranch two lines away; sh's reader prints `v.strip()`; policy.ts trims for its token. Three readers, one of them non-canonical.
- A whitespace-only string is TRUTHY in PowerShell, so `if (… -and $Settings.qualityGate)` gates, `if (-not $Command)` does not short-circuit, and record_check_run then refuses the blank command — which is why the symptom is a rescue ref on every completion rather than a quiet no-op.
- The ps1 gate-failure string is used for both the chat line and the add_comment body, so one edit satisfies both halves of DoD 3.
- Both parity lists pin the bare `PUSH-BLOCKED:` substring, which is exactly why the missing marker went unnoticed; pinning the marker closes that hole.
- The frozen suite's pushBlocked helper matches `includes('PUSH-BLOCKED')`, so a prefix does not disturb the existing arms — verify before relying on it.
- This project's own settings.qualityGate is empty, so the live fleet sees no behaviour change from the trim.
planningNotes.risks:
1. Honest reds: both new arms are red on ps1 only. On sh they pass from the start and are parity guards — reporting them as two-engine reds would be false evidence.
2. Emoji encoding: the marker must survive in the wrapper file and in both parity scripts under PS 5.1 as well as pwsh. A tool that rewrites the file in another encoding breaks the check on the other engine; verify with a run on each.
3. An over-eager trim could silently stop a legitimate gate from running — the `gate-padded` arm is what proves a padded but real command still runs.
4. Existing gate-failure arms must still match their PUSH-BLOCKED line now that it carries a marker.
5. postflight.sh is about 36 minutes and the ps1 twin must be launched from PowerShell, not Git Bash.
